messages:
alexa: Heads-up — we kicked off the 65B quantized bring-up across us-east, eu-west and ap-northeast. Need quick alignment for Dedicated sizing + autoscale headroom. TL;DR numbers below.

mike: Nice. Are these q4f16 numbers or q8?

alexa: q4f16 for the primary run; we included a q8 sanity run. Results are noisy in ap-northeast (warm caches matter).

tara: Can you paste the short perf table?

alexa: Sure — raw from bench-bot: ```
model: 65B-q4f16
region | GPU  | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/s/GPU | avg_concurrency_per_gpu
US-EAST | H100 80GB | 120 | 320 | 520 | 2200 | 12
EU-WEST | A100 80GB | 150 | 380 | 610 | 1850 | 10
AP-NE  | H100 80GB (spotty) | 130 | 450 | 900 | 1600 | 9
q8 run (us-east H100) p99 ~ 420 ms, tokens/s/GPU ~ 2400
```

sandeep: Hmm p99 900ms in ap-ne. Is that cold-start + KV warmup?

alexa: Yes, bench-bot annotated that ~60% of p99 tail there was cache-miss/warmup. Warmup experiment (prefetch prefix cache) cut AP-NE p99 to ~480ms.

mike: For Dedicated sizing we should plan on steady-state p99 excluding cold starts, but autoscale needs to cover warmup microbursts. Proposed concurrency target per GPU = 10 steady, headroom = 1.5x -> target cap 15. Thoughts?

tara: 1.5x headroom seems reasonable for normal diurnal surges. For cross-region failover we need an extra 20% reserved capacity in EU to handle US spillover in outage scenarios.

sandeep: Agree. Also mind kernel choice: cutlass-fused GEMM for H100 gave ~8% lower latency vs baseline. For A100 we should stick to the current triton kernel set — q4f16 performance was worse when forcing cutlass there.

bench-bot: run_id: 3076543205 — additional metrics: steady CPU overhead low, memory footprint ~42GB KV per GPU, cache warmup iterations ~6 for 2048-prefix.

alexa: Proposed Dedicated pool sizing (steady -> max with headroom): ```
region: us-east (H100) -> steady GPUs: 40 (concurrency 10) -> max w/headroom: 60
region: eu-west (A100) -> steady GPUs: 30 -> max w/headroom+failover reserve: 54 (30 * 1.5 * 1.2)
region: ap-northeast (H100) -> steady GPUs: 10 -> max w/headroom: 15
```

mike: Can we express this in QPS? If steady concurrency per GPU 10 and tokens/s/GPU 2200, then steady tokens/s = GPUs * 10 * ? Wait we double-count. Let's do requests/s (assume avg request = 60 tokens). tokens/s/GPU 2200 -> requests/s/GPU ~= 36.6 -> 40 GPUs -> ~1464 rps steady. Max w/headroom 60 GPUs -> ~2196 rps.

tara: Good call. We'll use rps for autoscale thresholds. Autoscale policy: scale-up at 85% of max rps sustained for 15s, scale-down at 40% for 90s.

sandeep: Ops note: make sure fallback model variant (smaller fp16 13B) is in routing policy for sustained overloads; we want graceful degradation vs hard errors. Also add a canary rollout for the quant model on Dedicated for first 48h.

alexa: Action items: 1) eng-platform to provision the above pools and set autoscale thresholds (mike). 2) eng-ml to run extended warmup + prefetch to verify AP-NE tail (tara). 3) bench to produce 24h synthetic burst sim (bench-bot). 4) ops to add routing fallback and canary policy (sandeep).

mike: I'll start the infra ticket and tag @billing to estimate cost delta (big H100 numbers).

bench-bot: scheduled: burst-sim-3076543220 -> will push synthetic 3x diurnal peak for 3 hours across regions.

alexa: Thanks, team. Will post updated perf sheet after 24h sim. :thumbsup:
